statements.text: Patient reports feeling really down for about three months.

evidence.quote: I've just been really down. For about three months now.

statements.text: Patient reports loss of interest in activities, no longer painting on weekends since June.

evidence.quote: I don't enjoy anything anymore. I used to paint on the weekends and I haven't touched it since June.

statements.text: Patient reports difficulty sleeping, falling asleep okay but waking around 4 a.m. and unable to return to sleep.

evidence.quote: Bad. I fall asleep okay, but I wake up around 4 in the morning and I can't get back to sleep.

statements.text: Patient reports decreased appetite and unintentional weight loss of about 8 pounds.

evidence.quote: I'm just not hungry. I think I've lost maybe 8 pounds without trying.

statements.text: Patient reports low energy all the time and difficulty concentrating at work.

evidence.quote: Low energy, all the time. At work I read the same email like three times.

statements.text: Patient identifies relationship ending in spring after five years as a possible stressor.

evidence.quote: My relationship ended in the spring. Five years. But honestly, it feels bigger than that now.

statements.text: Patient denies history of prior depression or anxiety treatment.

evidence.quote: No, this is the first time. I've never been on anything for it.

statements.text: Patient denies manic or hypomanic episodes.

evidence.quote: No, never.

statements.text: Patient reports family history: aunt on father's side has bipolar disorder; sister Paola takes medication for anxiety.

evidence.quote: My aunt on my dad's side has bipolar, I think. And my sister Paola takes something for anxiety, I don't know what.

statements.text: Patient denies suicidal thoughts or thoughts of self-harm.

evidence.quote: Have you had any thoughts that you'd be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No. I feel awful, but no, nothing like that.

statements.text: Patient denies thoughts of harming others.

evidence.quote: Any thoughts of hurting anyone else?
No.

statements.text: Patient reports alcohol use: about one glass of wine per week, no drug use.

evidence.quote: Maybe a glass of wine once a week. No drugs.

evidence.quote: I'm allergic to penicillin, I break out in hives.

statements.text: Start sertraline 25 mg orally once daily for one week, then increase to 50 mg orally once daily.

evidence.quote: What I'd like to do is start sertraline, 25 milligrams once a day for one week, then go up to 50 milligrams once a day.

evidence.quote: I'd also like you to start therapy, so I'm putting in a referral to our therapy team for weekly sessions.

note.after_visit_summary: You've been feeling down for about three months, with low energy, trouble sleeping, loss of interest in things you used to enjoy, and some weight loss. This sounds like moderate depression, which is treatable. We're starting a medication called sertraline: begin with 25 mg by mouth each day for one week, then increase to 50 mg each day. It may take 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full effect. Take it with breakfast. You're also being referred to therapy for weekly sessions. Keep the safety plan card we gave you; if you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, call or text 988 or go to the nearest emergency room. Return in 4 weeks on October 19th to check how the medication is working. Contact Lakeview Pharmacy pharmacy on 4120 Belmont Avenue for your prescription, and we can reach you at 773-555-0164.
